subject: error bars for nested data + separation of line segments (newbie)

messages.author: 3059821d711d3079
messages.subject: error bars for nested data + separation of line segments (newbie)
parts:
Dear Hadley et al. -- I am a relative newbie to R in the learning
phase of ggplot2 and, while amazed by its power and potential, am
having some difficulty coming up with the appropriate code for my
desired plot (trying to help out a colleague). Was hoping I could
get some input from the masters!

My (colleague's) data setup: rats nested within treatment groups,
responses then measured over time for each rat. Easy enough for me to
get the data in long format appropriate for, say, lme(), which I am
assuming is desirable for ggplot2 as well. Code below creates a
simplified version of the data I'm working with, though with random
values for the response that won't differ on average by group (while
the real data presumably will):

resp <- sample(100, replace=TRUE)
group <- rep(1:2, each=50)
rat <- rep(1:10, each=10)
time <- rep(1:10, length=100)
mydata <- data.frame(rat, group, time, resp)

1) main plot: I am interested in plotting time (x) against resp (y),
with one line per group, adding vertical error bars, lines and error
bars representing the mean and standard error for rats within that
group.

2) bonus feature: the first three time points per rat are a baseline,
so separating the line connecting those three with the line connecting
the rest of the time points would be wonderful. Obviously, I can code
baseline vs. experiment as a separate factor in the data if need be.

My desired plot seems quite similar to, say, Figure 5.15 (right panel)
from the ggplot2 book, but I am having difficulty translating the code
for that plot to suit my purposes. I imagine I need to use the
summary functions that access the Hmisc functions for standard errors,
but again, just am not yet "up to speed" enough to manage it on my
own. Taking into account the nesting (so that lines connects means of
groups rather than each rat) is tricky for me for some reason, though
I know it shouldn't be!

Many thanks in advance for any help/advice you can provide.

-Keith

messages.author: b756a7daa2c2aa6d
messages.subject: Re: error bars for nested data + separation of line segments (newbie)
parts:
Hi Keith,

Here's how I'd go about it - the key to both aspects of your problem
is setting up grouping correctly.

Hadley

resp <- sample(100, replace=TRUE)
group <- rep(1:2, each=50)
rat <- rep(1:10, each=10)
time <- rep(1:10, length=100)

rats <- data.frame(rat, group, time, resp)

library(ggplot2)
# Starting point
qplot(time, resp, data = rats)
# Split up by groups
qplot(time, resp, data = rats) +
facet_grid(~ group)
# Draw line for each rat
qplot(time, resp, data = rats, geom = "line", group = rat) +
facet_grid(~ group)
# Uhoh, bug in ggplot2 :( Work around:
rats$g <- rats$group
qplot(time, resp, data = rats, geom = "line", group = rat) +
facet_grid(~ g)

# Add mean lines and error bars
qplot(time, resp, data = rats, geom = "line", group = rat) +
facet_grid(~ g) +
stat_summary(aes(group = 1), fun.y = mean,
geom = "line", colour = "red") +
stat_summary(aes(group = time), fun.data = mean_cl_normal,
geom = "pointrange", colour = "red")
# The important thing to note in the above plot is the grouping:
# we want one line for each panel, so group = 1
# and error bars for each time, so time = 1

# To separate baseline points from treated, you use grouping
# in a similar way:
qplot(time, resp, data = rats, geom = "line",
group = interaction(rat, time <= 3)) + facet_grid(~ g)
